newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in featureless trade ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S., dealers said on Wednesday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), weekly jobless claims, October durable goods, November University of Michigan consumer sentiment index and November Chicago purchasing managers index (PMI) data.
The third-quarter GDP is forecast to show an increase of 1.7 percent compared with 2.2 percent reported in the previous quarter.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended November 23 is expected to ease to 336,000 against the previous week's 344,000.
Durable goods for October is expected to show a decline of 0.2 percent from September's 4.9 percent gain.
The University of Michigan consumer index for November is expected to rise to 98.0 percent versus October's 96.5 percent.
The Chicago November PMI is expected to ease to 55.1 percent against October's 56.9 percent.
"The market was quietly steady in the morning on the continued absence of fresh incentives," a local dealer said.
"The market is expecting a whole bunch of (U.S.) economic indicators tonight but the durable goods and Chicago PMI figures will be the most closely watched indicators," he said.

"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S," he added.

In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent. Thursday/Friday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-7/16 5-5/16 and week-fixed was unchanged at 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
